notes: Delete mirror of finance-replace-0019: removes the original rule; members reached only through it lose their answer, members stored by name keep it. R1: every current DJIA member (the 30 after the June 29, 2026 change, Coca-Cola and McDonald's among them) is headquartered in the United States; past members were not all (International Nickel / Inco, a component until 1987, had its head office in Toronto), so the rule is about today's members; the committee's guideline asks for U.S. incorporation and headquarters, with a clause letting it count a company as American by judgment, which no member uses. The questions ask the country, so headquarters moves within the U.S. (Boeing, Caterpillar) do not matter. Membership is contingent (the committee replaces members from time to time), so the by-name world, in which Coca-Cola or McDonald's leaves the Dow and stays headquartered in Atlanta or Chicago, contradicts no firm fact outside the chain; the member never stays in the Dow as an exception to the edited rule (README Decisions 2). Lopsided: both headquarters are stated by name very often. Worlds combine two independent storage choices. Derivability unlikely rather than very_unlikely: the rule is usually stated as '30 U.S. companies' rather than in the headquarters wording. No name leaks the answer ('Dow Jones' names people; 道琼斯 is a transliteration). The new members (Harrowgate Systems, Pellworth Health) are invented, so the rule is their only route. Near query: the number of members (30), not the edit's new value. Relation headquartered_in (functional) was used in ABox 0002 on a city; here it is a TBox rule over a country.
